questions.q: If two straight lines whose direction cosines are given by the relations $l + m - n = 0, 3l^{2} + m^{2} + cnl = 0$~are parallel, then the positive value of~$c$ is
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Given,& $l + m - n = 0$~&~$3l^{2} + m^{2} + cln = 0$

Now taking~$n = l + m$~and putting in~$3l^{2} + m^{2} + cln = 0$~we get,

$3l^{2} + m^{2} + cl\left(l + m\right) = 0$

$⇒ 3l^{2} + m^{2} + cl^{2} + clm = 0$

$⇒ \left(3 + c\right)l^{2} + clm + m^{2} = 0$

$⇒ \left(3 + c\right)\left(\dfrac{l}{m}\right)2 + c\left(\dfrac{l}{m}\right) + 1 = 0$~..equation (i)

$∵$~ lies are parallel.

So, roots of equation (i)~must be equal

$⇒ D = 0$

$⇒ c^{2} - 4\left(3 + c\right) = 0$

$⇒ c^{2} - 4c - 12 = 0$

$⇒ \left(c - 6\right)\left(c + 2\right) = 0$

$c = 6$~or~$c = - 2$

So, positive~value of~$c = 6$

questions.q: If the lines& $\dfrac{x - 1}{1} = \dfrac{y - 2}{2} = \dfrac{z + 3}{1}$~and~$\dfrac{x - a}{2} = \dfrac{y + 2}{3} = \dfrac{z - 3}{1}$~intersects at the point $P$, then~the distance of the point $P$ from the plane $z = a$ is :&
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Let

${L}_{1}: \dfrac{x - 1}{1} = \dfrac{y - 2}{2} = \dfrac{z + 3}{1} = \lambda$

Point on~${L}_{1} ≡ \left(\lambda +1, 2\lambda + 2, \lambda - 3\right)$

And,

${L}_{2}: $\dfrac{x - a}{2} = \dfrac{y + 2}{3} = \dfrac{z - 3}{1} = \mu

Point on~${L}_{2} ≡ \left(2\mu + a, 3\mu - 2, \mu + 3\right)$

For finding~$P$, we must have

$\lambda - 3 = \mu + 3 ⇒ \lambda = \mu + 6 . . . \left(i\right)$

$2\lambda + 2 = 3\mu - 2 ⇒ 2\lambda = 3\mu - 4 . . . \left($ii\right)$

Solving~ \left($i\right) \text{ and } \left($ii\right)$, we get

$\lambda = 22$~and~$\mu = 16$

Therefore,

$P ≡ \left($23, 46, 19\right)$

And,

$2\mu + a = \lambda + 1$

$⇒ 32 + a = 22 + 1$

$⇒ a = - 9$

Distance of point~$P \left($23, 46, 19\right)$~from the plane~$z + 9 = 0$~is

$= \left|$\dfrac{19 + 9}{{0}^{2} + {0}^{2} + {1}^{2}}\right| =28$& units

$

Given point $R$ lies on the line segment joining the points $P$ and $Q,$ hence direction ratios of the line

Hence, distance from origin $= \sqrt{16 + 4 + 36} = 2\sqrt{14}$

questions.q: Let the point A divide the line segment joining the points $P(-1,-1,2)$ and $Q(5,5,10)$ internally in the ratio $\mathrm{r}: 1(\mathrm{r}\gt0)$. If O is the origin and $(\overrightarrow{\mathrm{OQ}} \cdot \overrightarrow{\mathrm{OA}})-\frac{1}{5}|\overrightarrow{\mathrm{OP}} \times \overrightarrow{\mathrm{OA}}|^2=10$, then the value of r is :
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} & A=\left(\frac{5 r-1}{r+1}, \frac{5 r-1}{r+1}, \frac{10 r+2}{r+1}\right) \\ & (\overrightarrow{O Q} \cdot \overrightarrow{O A})-\frac{1}{5}|\overrightarrow{O P} \times \overrightarrow{O A}|^2=10 \\ & \overrightarrow{O Q}=5 \hat{i}+5 \hat{j}+10 \hat{k} \\ & \overrightarrow{O A}=\frac{5 r-1}{r+1} \hat{i}+\frac{5 r-1}{r+1} \hat{j}+\frac{10 r+2}{r+1} \hat{k} \\ & \overrightarrow{O P}=-\hat{i}-\hat{j}+2 \hat{k} \\ & \left.\overrightarrow{O P} \times \overrightarrow{O A}=\frac{1}{r+1} \right\rvert\, \frac{5 r-1}{5} \quad 5 r-1 \quad 10 r+2 \\ & =\frac{1}{r+1}(\hat{i}(20 r)-\hat{j}(20 r)) \\ & =5\left(\frac{5 r-1}{r+1}\right)+5\left(\frac{5 r-1}{r+1}\right)+10\left(\frac{10 r+2}{r+1}\right) \\ & \quad-\frac{1}{5}\left(\frac{2 \times 400 r^2}{(r+1)^2}\right)=10 \\ & \frac{150 r+10}{r+1}-\frac{1}{5}\left(\frac{2 \times 400 r^2}{(r+1)^2}\right)=10 \\ & (150 r+10)(r+1)-160 r^2=10(r+1)^2 \\ & (15 r+1)(r+1)-16 r^2=(r+1)^2 \\ & 15 r^2+16 r+1-16 r^2=r^2+2 r+1 \\ & -2 r^2+14 r=0\end{aligned}r=0,7$

questions.q: Let the position vectors of two points $P$ and $Q$~be $3\overset{^}{i} - \overset{^}{j} + 2\overset{^}{k}$ and $\overset{^}{i} + 2\overset{^}{j} - 4\overset{^}{k}$, respectively. Let~$R$ and $S$ be two points such that the direction ratios of lines $PR$ and $QS$ are  \left(4, - 1, 2\right)$~and~  \left(- 2, 1, - 2\right)$, respectively. Let lines $PR$ and $QS$ intersect at~$T$. If the vector $\overset{→}{TA}$ is perpendicular to both $\overset{→}{PR}$ and $\overset{→}{QS}$ and the length of vector $\overset{→}{TA}$~is $\sqrt{5}$ units, then the modulus of a position vector of $A$ is :
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
$P \left(3, - 1, 2\right)$

$Q \left(1, 2, - 4\right)$

$\overset{→}{PR} ‖ 4\overset{^}{i} - \overset{^}{j} + 2\overset{^}{k}$

$\overset{→}{QS} ‖ - 2\overset{^}{i} + \overset{^}{j} - 2\overset{^}{k}$

Dr's of normal to the plane containing~$P, T$~and~$Q$ will be proportional to :~

\left|\begin{cases}\overset{^}{i}& \overset{^}{j} & \overset{^}{k} \\ 4 & - 1 & 2 \\ - 2 & 1 & - 2\end{cases}\right| = 4\overset{^}{j} + 2\overset{^}{k}$

$∴ \dfrac{ℓ}{0} = \dfrac{m}{4} = \dfrac{n}{2}$

For point, $T$~:~$\overset{→}{PT} = \dfrac{x - 3}{4} = \dfrac{y + 1}{- 1} = \dfrac{z - 2}{2} = \lambda$

$\overset{→}{QT} = \dfrac{x - 1}{- 2} = \dfrac{y - 2}{1} = \dfrac{z + 4}{- 2} = \mu$

$T ≡ \left(4\lambda + 3, - \lambda - 1, 2\lambda + 2\right)$

$Q ≡ \left($2\mu + 1, \mu + 2, - 2\mu - 4\right)$

$4\lambda + 3 = - 2\mu + 1 ⇒ 2\lambda + \mu = - 1$

$\lambda + \mu = - 3 ⇒ \lambda = 2$

and~$\mu = - 5, \lambda + \mu = - 3 ⇒ \lambda = 2$

So point $T: \left($11, - 3, 6\right)$

$\overset{→}{OA} = \left($11\overset{^}{i} - 3\overset{^}{j} + 6\overset{^}{k}\right)$\pm \left(\dfrac{2\overset{^}{j} + \overset{^}{k}}{5}\right)\sqrt{5}

$\overset{→}{OA} = \left($11\overset{^}{i} - 3\overset{^}{j} + 6\overset{^}{k}\right)$\pm \left($2\overset{^}{j} + \overset{^}{k}\right)$

$\overset{→}{OA} = 11\overset{^}{i} - \overset{^}{j} + 7\overset{^}{k}$~or~$9\overset{^}{i} - 5\overset{^}{j} + 5\overset{^}{k}$

\left|\overset{→}{OA}\right| = $\sqrt{121 + 1 + 49} = \sqrt{171}$or~$\sqrt{81 + 25 + 25} = \sqrt{131}$

questions.q: The direction ratios of normal to the plane through the points (0,-1,0) and (0,0,1) and making an angle $\frac{\pi}{4}$ with the plane $y-z+5=0$ are; 2,-1,1 $2, \sqrt{2}-\sqrt{2}\sqrt{2}, 1,-12 \sqrt{3}, 1,-1$
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution: Let the d.r's of the normal be $\langle a, b, c\rangle$ Equation of the plane is $a(x-0)+b(y+1)+c(z-0)=0\because$ It passes through (0,0,1) $\therefore \quad b+c=0$ Also $\frac{0 \cdot a+b-c}{\sqrt{a^{2}+b^{2}+c^{2} \cdot \sqrt{2}}}=\cos \frac{\pi}{4}=\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\Rightarrow \quad b-c=\sqrt{a^{2}+b^{2}+c^{2}}$ And $b+c=0\Rightarrow \quad b=\pm \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}} a\therefore \quad$ The d.r's are $\sqrt{2}, 1,-1$ or $2, \sqrt{2},-\sqrt{2}$

questions.q: The position vectors of the vertices $A, B$ and $C$ of a triangle are $2\overset{^}{i} - 3\overset{^}{j} + 3\overset{^}{k}, 2\overset{^}{i} + 2\overset{^}{j} + 3\overset{^}{k}$ and $- \overset{^}{i} + \overset{^}{j} + 3\overset{^}{k}$ respectively. Let $l$ denotes the length of the angle bisector $AD$ of $∠ BAC$ where $D$ is on the line segment $BC$, then $2l^{2}$ equals :
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Given: $A \left(2, - 3, 3\right), B \left($2, 2, 3\$right)\$ttext{and}C\left(-$1, 1, 3\right)$ are vertices of a $△ ABC$.

$AB = \sqrt{\left(2 - 2\right)2 + \left(2 + 3\right)2 + \left(3 - 3\right)2}$

$⇒ AB = 5$

$⇒ AC = \sqrt{\left(2 + 1\right)2 + \left(- 3 - 1\right)2 + \left(3 - 3\right)2}$

$⇒ AC = \sqrt{9 + 16}$

$⇒ AC = 5$

Also, $AD$ is the angle bisector of $∠ BAC$.

$⇒ \dfrac{AB}{AC} = \dfrac{BD}{CD}$

$⇒ BD = CD$

$∴D$ is midpoint of $BC$

So, using mid-point formula,

$⇒ D ≡ $\$left(\dfrac{2 - 1}{2}, \dfrac{2 + 1}{2}, \dfrac{3 + 3}{2}\right)

$⇒ D ≡ $\$left(\dfrac{1}{2}, \dfrac{3}{2},$3\right)$

$⇒ AD = l = $\sqrt{\left(2 - \dfrac{1}{2}\right)2 + \left(- 3 - \dfrac{3}{2}\right)2 + ( 3 - 3{)}^{2}}

$⇒ l = $\sqrt{\left(\dfrac{3}{2}\right)2 + \left(- \dfrac{9}{2}\right)2}

$⇒ l = $\sqrt{\dfrac{9}{4} + \dfrac{81}{4}}

$⇒ l = $\sqrt{\dfrac{45}{2}}

$⇒ l^{2} = $\dfrac{45}{2}

$⇒ 2l^{2} = 45$

$

questions.q: The line ${l}_{1}$~passes through the point  \left(2, 6, 2\right)$ and is perpendicular to the plane $2x + y - 2z = 10$. Then the shortest distance between the line ${l}_{1}$~and the line $\dfrac{x + 1}{2} = \dfrac{y + 4}{- 3} = \dfrac{z}{2}$ is:$
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
The line& ${l}_{1}$~passes through the point~$( 2, 6, 2 )$~and~is perpendicular to the line~$2x + y - 2z = 10$~then,

${l}_{1}: \dfrac{x - 2}{2} = \dfrac{y - 6}{1} = \dfrac{z - 2}{- 2}$~

Let the shortest distance between~${l}_{1}$~and the line~$\dfrac{x + 1}{2} = \dfrac{y + 4}{- 3} = \dfrac{z}{2}$~is~S.D.

S.D.~$= \left|\overset{→}{AB} \cdot \overset{→}{MN}\left|\overset{→}{MN}\right|\right|$

Here,~$\overset{→}{AB} = 3\overset{^}{i} + 10\overset{^}{j} + 2\overset{^}{k}$

$\overset{→}{MN} = \left|\begin{cases}\overset{^}{i} & \overset{^}{j} & \overset{^}{k} \\ 2 & 1 & - 2 \\ 2 & - 3 & 2\end{cases}\right| = - 4\overset{^}{i} - 8\overset{^}{j} - 8\overset{^}{k}$

$⇒ \left|\overset{→}{MN}\right| = \sqrt{16 + 64 + 64} = 12$

$\overset{→}{AB} \cdot \overset{→}{MN} = - 12 - 80 - 16 = - 108$

So, shortest distance (S.D.)~

$= \left|\dfrac{- 108}{12}\right| = \left|- 9\right| = 9$& units

questions.q: Let $\alpha$ be the angle between the lines whose direction cosines satisfy the equations $l + m - n = 0$~and $l^{2} + m^{2} - n^{2} = 0$. Then the value of $\sin^{4}\alpha + \cos^{4}\alpha$ is :
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
$n = ℓ + m$

Now,~${ℓ}^{2} + m^{2} = n^{2} = \left(ℓ + m\right)2$

$⇒ 2ℓm = 0$

$l^{2} + m^{2} + n^{2} = 1$

If $ℓ = 0 ⇒ 2n^{2} = 1 ⇒ n = \pm \dfrac{1}{2}$

$m = n = \pm \dfrac{1}{2}$

And, If $m = 0 ⇒ n = ℓ = \pm \dfrac{1}{2}$

$∴ l^{2} + m^{2} = \dfrac{1}{2} \text{ and } l + m = \dfrac{1}{2}$

$⇒ \dfrac{1}{2} + 2 lm = \dfrac{1}{2}$

$∴ l = 0, m = \dfrac{1}{2}$~or~$l = \dfrac{1}{2}, m = 0$

So, direction cosines of two lines are

\left(0, \dfrac{1}{2}, \dfrac{1}{2}\right)$~and~ \left(\dfrac{1}{2}, 0, \dfrac{1}{2}\right)$

Thus,

$∴ cos\alpha = 0 + 0 + \dfrac{1}{2} = \dfrac{1}{2}$

$⇒ \alpha = \dfrac{π}{3}$

$∴ \sin^{4}\alpha + \cos^{4}\alpha = 1 - \dfrac{1}{2}\sin^{2} ( 2\alpha ) = 1 - \dfrac{1}{2} \cdot \dfrac{3}{4} = \dfrac{5}{8}$

questions.q: Let the position vectors of the vertices $A, B$ and $C$ of a triangle be $2\overset{^}{i} + 2\overset{^}{j} + \overset{^}{k}, \overset{^}{i} + 2\overset{^}{j} + 2\overset{^}{k}$ and $2\overset{^}{i} + \overset{^}{j} + 2\overset{^}{k}$ respectively. Let ${l}_{1}, {l}_{2}$ and ${l}_{3}$ be the lengths of perpendiculars drawn from the ortho centre of the triangle on the sides $AB, BC$ and $CA$ respectively, then ${l}_{1}^{2} + {l}_{2}^{2} + {l}_{3}^{2}$ equals :
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Given: $A \left(2, 2, 1\right), B \left($1, 2, 2\$right)\$ttext{and}C\left($2, 1, 2\right)$ are vertices of $∆ ABC$.

$⇒ AB = \sqrt{\left(2 - 1\right)2 + \left(2 - 2\right)2 + \left(1 - 2\right)2} = \sqrt{2}$

$⇒ BC = \sqrt{\left(1 - 2\right)2 + \left(2 - 1\right)2 + \left(2 - 2\right)2} = \sqrt{2}$

$⇒ CA = \sqrt{\left(2 - 2\right)2 + \left(2 - 1\right)2 + \left(1 - 2\right)2} = \sqrt{2}$

So, $∆ ABC$ is equilateral.

Therefore, orthocentre and centroid will be same.

$⇒ G ≡ $\$left(\dfrac{2 + 1 + 2}{3}, \dfrac{2 + 2 + 1}{3}, \dfrac{1 + 2 + 2}{3}\right)

$⇒ G ≡ \$left(\dfrac{5}{3}, \dfrac{5}{3}, \dfrac{5}{3}\right)$

Also, mid point of $AB$ is $D $\$left(\dfrac{3}{2},$2, $\dfrac{3}{2}\right)

$⇒ {l}_{1} = $\sqrt{\left(\dfrac{3}{2} - \dfrac{5}{3}\right)2 + \left(2 - \dfrac{5}{3}\right)2 + \left(\dfrac{3}{2} - \dfrac{5}{3}\right)2}

$⇒ {l}_{1} = $\sqrt{\dfrac{1}{36} + \dfrac{1}{9} + \dfrac{1}{36}}

$⇒ {l}_{1} = $\sqrt{\dfrac{1}{6}}

Similarly, ${l}_{2} = {l}_{3} = $\sqrt{\dfrac{1}{6}}

$⇒ \left({l}_{1}\right)2 + \left({l}_{2}\right)2 + \left({l}_{3}\right)2 = $\dfrac{1}{6} + \dfrac{1}{6} + \dfrac{1}{6}

$⇒ \left({l}_{1}\right)2 + \left({l}_{2}\right)2 + \left({l}_{3}\right)2 = $\dfrac{1}{2}

$

questions.q: If the length of the perpendicular drawn from the point $P\left(a, 4, 2\right), a > 0$~on the line $\dfrac{x + 1}{2} = \dfrac{y - 3}{3} = \dfrac{z - 1}{- 1}$~is~$2\sqrt{6}$~units and $Q \left({α}_{1}, {α}_{2}, {α}_{3}\right)~is the image of the point $P$ in this line, then $a + \mathop{∑}_{i = 1}^{3}{α}_{i}$ \text{ and } is equal to$
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Let a point on the line& $\dfrac{x + 1}{2} = \dfrac{y - 3}{3} = \dfrac{z - 1}{- 1} = \lambda$~be

$M \left(2\lambda - 1, 3\lambda + 3, - \lambda + 1\right)$

and the~DR's of the line are~\left<2, 3, - 1\right>$

The DR's of line joining the points~ \left(2\lambda - 1, 3\lambda + 3, - \lambda + 1\right)$~and~ \left(a, 4, 2\right)$~will be

\left<2\lambda - 1 - a, 3\lambda - 1, - \lambda - 1\right>$

Now its perpendicular to the given line, so \left($2\lambda - 1 - a\right)2 + \left($3\lambda - 1\right)3 + \left(- \lambda -$1\right)\left(-$1\right) = 0$

$⇒ 4\lambda - 2 - 2a + 9\lambda - 3 + \lambda + 1 = 0$

$⇒ 14\lambda - 4 - 2a = 0$

$⇒ 7\lambda - 2 - a = 0 ⇒ 7\lambda - 2 = a$

and,

\left($2\lambda - 1 - a\right)2 + \left($3\lambda - 1\right)2 + \left(\lambda +$1\right)2 = \left($2\sqrt{6}\right)2$

$⇒ \left($5\lambda - 1\right)2 + \left($3\lambda - 1\right)2 + \left(\lambda + 1\right)2 = 24$

$⇒ 35{λ}^{2} - 14\lambda - 21 = 0$

$⇒ \left(\lambda - 1\right) \left(35\lambda + 21\right) = 0$

For,~$\lambda = 1; a = 5$

i.e.~$M ≡ \left(1, 6, 0\right)$

As~$Q \left({α}_{1}, {α}_{2}, {α}_{3}\right)~is the image~of point~$P$

\begin{cases}\dfrac{{α}_{1} + 5}{2} =$1; & $\dfrac{{α}_{2} + 4}{2} =$6; & $\dfrac{{α}_{3} + 2}{2} =$0\end{cases}$

$⇒ $\begin{cases}{α}_{1} = -$3; & {α}_{2} = 8; & {α}_{3} = - 2\end{cases}$

Hence,~$a + {α}_{1} + {α}_{2} + {α}_{3} = 8$

$

questions.q: Each of the angles $\beta$ and $\gamma$ that a given line makes with the positive y - and z -axes, respectively, is half of the angle that this line makes with the positive x -axes. Then the sum of all possible values of the angle $\beta$ is
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
$\begin{aligned}
& \beta=\frac{\alpha}{2}, \gamma=\frac{\alpha}{2} \\ & \cos ^2 \alpha+\cos ^2 \beta+\cos ^2 \gamma=1 \\ & \cos ^2 \alpha+2 \cos ^2 \frac{\alpha}{2}=1 \\ & \cos ^2 \alpha+\cos \alpha=0 \\ & \cos \alpha(\cos \alpha+1)=0 \\ & \cos \alpha=0,-1 \\ & \alpha=\frac{\pi}{2}, \pi
\end{aligned}$
Now $\beta=\frac{\alpha}{2} \Rightarrow \frac{\pi}{4}, \frac{\pi}{2}$
so sum is $\frac{3 \pi}{4}$

questions.q: Let $O$ be the origin and the position vector of $A$ and $B$ be $2\overset{^}{i} + 2\overset{^}{j} + \overset{^}{k}$ and $2\overset{^}{i} + 4\overset{^}{j} + 4\overset{^}{k}$ respectively. If the internal bisector of $∠ AOB$ meets the line $AB$ at $C$, then the length of $OC$ is
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
We know that, the internal bisector divides base in the same ratio as the two remaining sides.

$⇒ \dfrac{OA}{OB} = \dfrac{AC}{BC}$

$⇒ \dfrac{{2}^{2} + {2}^{2} + {1}^{2}}{{2}^{2} + {4}^{2} + {4}^{2}} = \dfrac{AC}{BC}$

$⇒ \dfrac{3}{6} = \dfrac{AC}{BC}$

$⇒ AC: BC = 1: 2$

$⇒ C ≡ \left(\dfrac{1 \times 2 + 2 \times 2}{3}, \dfrac{1 \times 4 + 2 \times 2}{3}, \dfrac{1 \times 4 + 2 \times 1}{3}\right)$

$⇒ C ≡ \left(2, $\dfrac{8}{3},$2\right)$

$⇒ OC = $\sqrt{{2}^{2} + \left(\dfrac{8}{3}\right)2 + {2}^{2}}

$⇒ OC = $\sqrt{8 + \dfrac{64}{9}} = \dfrac{136}{3}

$⇒ OC = \dfrac{2\sqrt{34}}{3}$

$

questions.q: The length of the perpendicular from the point  \left(1, - 2, 5\right)$~on the line passing through  \left(1, 2, 4\right)$~and parallel to the line $x + y - z = 0 = x - 2y + 3z - 5$& is:
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Given line is parallel to the line $x + y - z = 0 = x - 2y + 3z - 5$~is:

So, direction ratio~of the line~$= \left|\begin{cases}\overset{^}{i} & \overset{^}{j} & \overset{^}{k} \\ 1 & 1 & - 1 \\ 1 & - 2 & 3\end{cases}\right| = \overset{^}{i} - 4\overset{^}{j} - 3\overset{^}{k}$

So, equation of line passing through~ \left(1, 2, 4\right)$~is

$\overset{→}{r} = \overset{^}{i} + 2\overset{^}{j} + 4\overset{^}{k} + \lambda \left(\overset{^}{i} -4\overset{^}{j} - 3\overset{^}{k}\right)$

Let~$A \left(1, 2, 4\right)$,$Q \left(1, - 2, 5\right)$~and~$P$~be~ \left($1 + \lambda, 2 - 4\lambda, 4 - 3\lambda\right)$

Given $\overset{→}{PQ}$~and line are perpendicular,

So,~$\overset{→}{PQ} $\cdot \left(\overset{^}{i} -$4\overset{^}{j} - 3\overset{^}{k}\right) = 0$

$⇒ \left(\lambda\overset{^}{i} + \left($4 - 4\lambda\right)\overset{^}{j} - \left($1 + 3\lambda\right)\overset{^}{k}\right) . \left(\overset{^}{i} -$4\overset{^}{j} - 3\overset{^}{k}\right) = 0$

$⇒ \lambda - 16 + 16\lambda + 3 + 9\lambda = 0$

$⇒ \lambda = \dfrac{13}{26} = \dfrac{1}{2}$

Hence~$\overset{→}{PQ} ≡ \left(\dfrac{1}{2},2, \dfrac{- 5}{2}\right)$

Now~\left|PQ\right| = \sqrt{\dfrac{21}{2}}$

$

questions.q: Let a line pass through two distinct points $P(-2,-1,3)$ and $Q$, and be parallel to the vector $3 \hat{i}+2 \hat{j}+2 \hat{k}$. If the distance of the point Q from the point $\mathrm{R}(1,3,3)$ is 5 , then the square of the area of $\triangle P Q R$ is equal to :
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Equation of line $P Q$ is: $\frac{x+2}{3}=\frac{y+1}{2}=\frac{z-3}{2}=r(\text { say })$ Let coordinate of $Q=(3 r-2,2 r-1,2 r+3)\because P R=5$ Then $\begin{aligned} & (3 r-2-1)^2+(2 r-1-3)^2+(2 r+3-3)^2=25 \\ & \therefore r=0 \text { or } 2 \\ & \therefore \quad \text { Coordinate of } Q=(4,3,7) \end{aligned}$
$\begin{aligned} \therefore & \text { square of area of } \triangle P Q R=\left|\frac{1}{2}(\overrightarrow{P Q} \times \overrightarrow{P R})\right|^2 \\ & =\left|\frac{1}{2}(6 \hat{i}+4 \hat{j}+4 \hat{k}) \times(3 \hat{i}+4 \hat{j})\right|^2 \\ & =|-8 \hat{i}+6 \hat{j}+6 \hat{k}|^2=136\end{aligned}$

questions.q: The projection of the line segment joining the point  \left(1, - 1, 3\right)$ and  \left(2, - 4, 11\right)$ on the line joining the points  \left(- 1, 2, 3\right)$ and  \left(3, - 2,10\right)$ is _______
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Let A \left(1, - 1,3\right)$ , B \left(2, - 4, 11\right)$
$\overset{→}{AB} = \overset{^}{i} - 3\overset{^}{j} + 8\overset{^}{k}$
C \left(- 1, 2, 3\right)$ , D \left(3, - 2, 10\right)$
$\overset{→}{CD} = 4\overset{^}{i} - 4\overset{^}{j} + 7\overset{^}{k}$
Projection of $\overset{→}{AB}$ on $\overset{→}{CD}= \dfrac{\overset{→}{AB} . \overset{→}{CD}}{\left|\overset{→}{CD}\right|} = \left(\dfrac{4 + 12 + 56}{\sqrt{16 + 16 + 49}}\right) = \dfrac{72}{9} = 8$

questions.q:
A line $l$ passing through origin is perpendicular to the lines

${l}_{1}: \overset{→}{r} = \left(3 + t\right)\overset{^}{i} + \left(- 1 + 2t\right)\overset{^}{j} + \left(4 + 2t\right)\overset{^}{k}$

${l}_{2}: \overset{→}{r} = \left(3 + 2s\right)\overset{^}{i} + \left(3 + 2s\right)\overset{^}{j} + \left(2 + s\right)\overset{^}{k}$

If the co-ordinates of the point in the first octant on ${l}_{2}$ at a distance of $\sqrt{17}$ from the point of intersection of $l$ and ${l}_{1}$ are \left(a, b, c\right)$,~then $18 \left(a + b + c\right)$ is equal to ___ .

$
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
${l}_{1}: \overset{→}{r} = \left(3 + t\right)\overset{^}{i} + \left(- 1 + 2t\right)\overset{^}{j} + \left(4 + 2t\right)\overset{^}{k}$

${l}_{2}: \overset{→}{r} = \left(3 + 2s\right)\overset{^}{i} + \left(3 + 2s\right)\overset{^}{j} + \left(2 + s\right)\overset{^}{k}$

$DR$~of ${l}_{1} ≡ \left(1, 2, 2\right)$

$DR$~of ${l}_{2} ≡ \left(2, 2, 1\right)$

${l}_{1} \times {l}_{2} = \left|\begin{cases}i & j & k \\ 1 & 2 & 2 \\ 2 & 2 & 1\end{cases}\right|$

$= i \left(2 - 4\right) - j \left($1 - 4\right) + $k\left($2 - 4\right)$

$= - 2i + 3j - 2k$

Hence,~$DR$~of $l$~( line $⊥$ to ${l}_{1} \text{ and } {l}_{2}$)

$= \left(-$2, 3, - 2\right)$

$∴ l: \overset{→}{r} = - 2\mu\overset{^}{i} + 3\mu\overset{^}{j} - 2\mu\overset{^}{k}$

for intersection of $l \text{ and } {l}_{1}$

$3 + t = - 2\mu$

$- 1 + 2t = 3\mu$

$4 + 2t = - 2\mu$

$⇒ t = - 1 \text{ and } \mu = - 1$

$∴$ Point of intersection $P ≡ \left($2, - 3, 2\right)$

Let point on ${l}_{2}$ be $Q \left($3 + 2s, 3 + 2s, 2 + s\right)$

Given~$PQ = $\sqrt{17}$⇒ \left($PQ\right)2 = 17$

$⇒ \left($2s + 1\right)2 + \left($6 + 2s\right)2 + \left($s\right)2 = 17$

$⇒ 9s^{2} + 28s + 20 = 0$

$⇒ s = - 2, - $\dfrac{10}{9}

$s \ne - 2$~as point lies on ${1}^{st}$ octant.

$∴ a = 3 + 2\left(- \dfrac{10}{9}\right) = \dfrac{7}{9}

$b = 3 + 2\left(- \dfrac{10}{9}\right) = \dfrac{7}{9}

$c = 2 + \left(- \dfrac{10}{9}\right) = \dfrac{8}{9}

$∴ 18\left($a + b + c\right) = 18$\$left(\dfrac{22}{9}\right) =44$

$

questions.q: Let $P  \left(-2, - 1, 1\right)$ and $Q \left(\dfrac{56}{17}, \dfrac{43}{17}, \dfrac{111}{17}\right)be the vertices of the rhombus $PRQS$. If the direction ratios of the diagonal $RS$ are \alpha, -$1, $\beta,where both \alphaand \betaare integers of minimum absolute values, then ${α}^{2} + {β}^{2}$ is equal to$
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Given,

& $P \left(-2, - 1, 1\right)$ and $Q \left(\dfrac{56}{17}, \dfrac{43}{17}, \dfrac{111}{17}\right)be the vertices of the rhombus $PRQS$. If the direction ratios of the diagonal $RS$ are \alpha, -$1, $\beta,where both \alphaand \beta~are integers of minimum absolute values, then ${α}^{2} + {β}^{2}$ is equal to

Now~$RS = \left(\alpha, -1, \beta\right)$

So, direction ratio~of~$PQ ≡ $\$left(\dfrac{56}{17} +$2, $\dfrac{43}{17} +$1, $\dfrac{111}{17} -$1\right)$

$≡ \$left(\dfrac{90}{17}, \dfrac{60}{17}, \dfrac{94}{17}\right)$

Now we know that diagonal of rhombus are perpendicular,

So,~$\dfrac{90}{17}\alpha + \dfrac{60}{17}\left(-1\right) + \dfrac{94}{17}\beta =0$

$⇒ $90\alpha +$+94\beta =$60$

$⇒ $\beta = \dfrac{60 - 90\alpha}{94}

$⇒ $\beta = \dfrac{30\left(2 - 3\alpha\right)}{94}

$⇒ $\beta = -$30 \$lleft(3\alpha -$2\right)94$

$⇒ $\beta = $\dfrac{- 15}{47}\llleft(3\alpha -2\right)$

$⇒ \dfrac{β}{- 15} = \dfrac{3\alpha - 2}{47}$

$⇒ \beta = -15, \alpha = -15$~ \left\${\text{as}\alpha\text{&}\beta\text{are integer}\right$\}$

So,~${α}^{2} + {β}^{2} = 225 + 225= 450$

$

questions.q: If the shortest distance between the line joining the points  \left(1, 2, 3\right)$~and  \left(2, 3, 4\right)$, and the line $\dfrac{x - 1}{2} = \dfrac{y + 1}{- 1} = \dfrac{z - 2}{0}$ is $\alpha$, then $28{α}^{2}$& is equal to _____ .
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Equation of line joining& \left(1, 2, 3\right)$~and~ \left(2, 3, 4\right)$~is

$\overset{→}{r} = \left(\overset{^}{i} + 2\overset{^}{j} + 3\overset{^}{k}\right) + \lambda \left(\overset{^}{i} + \overset{^}{j} + \overset{^}{k}\right)

Also, vector equation is

$\overset{→}{r} = \left(\overset{^}{i} - \overset{^}{j} +$2\overset{^}{k}\right) + \mu \left(2\overset{^}{i} - \overset{^}{j}\right)$

So,

$\overset{→}{a}1 = \left(\overset{^}{i} +2\overset{^}{j} + 3\overset{^}{k}\right)$

$\overset{→}{a}2 = \left(\overset{^}{i} - \overset{^}{j} +2\overset{^}{k}\right)$

Hence,

$\overset{→}{a}2 - \overset{→}{a}1 = 0\overset{^}{i} - 3\overset{^}{j} - \overset{^}{k}$

And,

$\overset{→}{b}1 = \overset{^}{i} + \overset{^}{j} + \overset{^}{k}$

$\overset{→}{b}2 = 2\overset{^}{i} - \overset{^}{j} + 0\overset{^}{k}$

And,~

$\overset{→}{b}1 \times \overset{→}{b}2 = \left|\begin{cases}\overset{^}{i}& \overset{^}{j} & \overset{^}{k} \\ 1 & 1 & 1 \\ 2 & - 1 & 0\end{cases}\right| = \overset{^}{i} + 2\overset{^}{j} - 3\overset{^}{k}$

$⇒ \left|\overset{→}{b}1 \times \overset{→}{b}2\right| = \sqrt{14}$

Required shortest distance is

$\alpha = \left|\left(\overset{→}{a}$2 - \overset{→}{a}1\$right)\cdot \left(\overset{→}{b}$1 $\times \overset{→}{b}$2\right)\right|\left|\overset{→}{b}$1 $\times \overset{→}{b}$2\right|$

$⇒ $\alpha = \left|$\dfrac{\left(- 3\overset{^}{j} - \overset{^}{k}\right) \cdot \left(\overset{^}{i} + 2\overset{^}{j} - 3\overset{^}{k}\right)}{14}\right|$

$⇒ $\alpha = \left|$\dfrac{- 6 + 3}{14}\right| = \dfrac{3}{14}$

Now, $28{α}^{2} = 228 $\times $\dfrac{9}{14} =18$.

$
